report.query: What evaluation methods exist for LLM reasoning agents?

per_paper_summaries.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
per_paper_summaries.one_sentence_summary: AgentBench introduces a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLMs as autonomous agents, focusing on integrated agent behavior across various environments.

per_paper_summaries.title: A Survey on Large Language Model based Autonomous Agents
per_paper_summaries.one_sentence_summary: This survey provides a unified conceptual framework for understanding LLM-based autonomous agents and highlights key open challenges in the field.

per_paper_summaries.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
per_paper_summaries.one_sentence_summary: Chain-of-thought prompting enhances LLM reasoning by employing reasoning chains in prompts, significantly improving multi-step reasoning task performance.

per_paper_summaries.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
per_paper_summaries.one_sentence_summary: ReAct integrates reasoning and acting in LLMs, enabling them to dynamically update context and self-correct based on observations, outperforming separate reasoning and acting models.

per_paper_summaries.title: OpenAgents: An Open Platform for Language Agents in the Wild
per_paper_summaries.one_sentence_summary: OpenAgents provides an infrastructure and tools for deploying and researching LLM agents in real-world settings, facilitating large-scale and reproducible research.

overlaps.description: Both papers address the lack of standardized evaluation and conceptual frameworks for LLM-based autonomous agents.
Both papers involve methods that enhance reasoning in language models, with Chain-of-Thought prompting and ReAct interleaving reasoning with actions.

differences.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
differences.description: AgentBench introduces a comprehensive benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs as autonomous agents across multiple environments, focusing on integrated agent behavior rather than isolated capabilities.

differences.title: A Survey on Large Language Model based Autonomous Agents
differences.description: This survey provides a unified conceptual framework for understanding LLM-based autonomous agents and identifies open challenges in the field, offering a broad overview rather than a specific technical solution.

differences.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
differences.description: The paper introduces chain-of-thought prompting, a method that enhances reasoning in LLMs by using reasoning chains in prompts, significantly improving performance on multi-step reasoning tasks.

differences.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
differences.description: ReAct combines reasoning and acting in a single framework, allowing LLMs to dynamically update context and self-correct based on observations, which is a novel approach compared to separate reasoning and acting methods.

differences.title: OpenAgents: An Open Platform for Language Agents in the Wild
differences.description: OpenAgents provides an open platform for deploying LLM agents in real-world settings, offering infrastructure and tools for large-scale, reproducible research on language agents beyond traditional benchmarks.

gaps.problem_formulation: The lack of standardized evaluation for LLM-based agents, which currently focus on isolated capabilities rather than integrated agent behavior.
gaps.description: While the problem of evaluating LLM-based agents is addressed through the creation of benchmarks like AgentBench, there is no exploration of using chain-of-thought prompting as a method to potentially enhance the evaluation process by incorporating reasoning capabilities directly into the evaluation criteria.
gaps.supporting_evidence: AgentBench focuses on creating a comprehensive benchmark but does not explore methods like chain-of-thought prompting that could integrate reasoning into the evaluation.

gaps.problem_formulation: Large language models often fail at multi-step reasoning tasks.
gaps.description: The problem of multi-step reasoning failures in LLMs is addressed through chain-of-thought prompting, but there is no exploration of how deploying these models on an open platform like OpenAgents could impact their reasoning capabilities in real-world applications.
gaps.supporting_evidence: Chain-of-thought prompting is used to improve reasoning, but there is no mention of deploying these models on platforms like OpenAgents to test reasoning improvements in real-world settings.

gaps.problem_formulation: Existing approaches separate reasoning and acting in language models, which limits their ability to dynamically update context and self-correct based on observations.
gaps.description: ReAct addresses the separation of reasoning and acting by combining them, but there is no evidence of using comprehensive benchmarks like AgentBench to evaluate the effectiveness of this integration across diverse environments.
gaps.supporting_evidence: ReAct combines reasoning and acting but does not utilize comprehensive benchmarks like AgentBench to evaluate its performance across multiple environments.

gaps.problem_formulation: Most LLM agent research evaluates on benchmarks without production deployment infrastructure.
gaps.description: While OpenAgents provides a platform for real-world deployment, there is no mention of using a unified conceptual framework to guide the deployment and evaluation of LLM agents in production environments.
gaps.supporting_evidence: OpenAgents focuses on deployment infrastructure but lacks a unified framework to guide the evaluation and deployment process.

report.synthesis: The corpus collectively highlights the need for standardized evaluation methods for LLM-based reasoning agents, as demonstrated by the introduction of benchmarks like AgentBench and the unified framework proposed in the survey of autonomous agents. Techniques such as chain-of-thought prompting and ReAct offer promising methods for enhancing reasoning capabilities and integrating reasoning with acting. However, there remains a gap in evaluating these advancements using comprehensive benchmarks across diverse environments and in real-world applications, as well as incorporating reasoning enhancements like chain-of-thought into evaluation criteria. Additionally, while platforms like OpenAgents provide necessary infrastructure for deployment, their integration with conceptual frameworks and benchmarks requires further exploration.
